Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the HealthSpan Hospitals Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HealthSpan Hospitals' financial results for the second quarter. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; Karen Walsh, Chief Strategy Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Information Officer; David Lee, Chief Human Resources Officer; and Monica Ruiz, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on eight key aspects: initiatives to improve operating margin, operating margin by segment, impact of acuity mix changes on revenue, revenue per admission trends and drivers, status of ongoing or planned acquisitions and divestitures, same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter and year, strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year, and factors affecting operating margin.

These aspects highlight our progress across the board, positioning us strongly for continued growth. Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Reynolds. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Reynolds mentioned, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter was $2.75 billion, an increase of 7.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives, and the impact of our strategic acquisitions.

Our operating expenses were $2.42 billion, representing 88% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $325 million, or $1.35 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and are raising our guidance for the full year.

Let me dive deeper into these results, starting with our initiatives to improve operating margin. Our operating margin expansion reached 11.8% in Q2, up 210 basis points year-over-year from 9.7% and 80 basis points sequentially from Q1. This marks our strongest quarterly margin in three years, driven by a multi-pronged strategy from our 2023 turnaround plan. For context, our consolidated operating margin now stands at 10.9% for the trailing twelve months, ahead of the acute care peer median of 9.2% per Kaufman Hall's National Hospital Flash Report, and closing in on high-performers like HCA Healthcare at 12.5%.

Our goal is to deliver 13-15% operating margins sustainably by fiscal 2026, despite headwinds like wage inflation—nursing RN rates 15-20% above 2019 levels—and CMS's FY2025 IPPS update with a 2.9% payment increase but 0.5% trim to DSH adjustments. Our four core pillars are revenue optimization, supply chain leverage, labor productivity, and clinical efficiency.

On revenue optimization, we're enhancing payer mix and CMI. Net revenue per adjusted patient day rose 4.2% year-over-year to $2,450, with a 150 basis point shift to commercial payers at 48%. In Sunbelt markets—Florida, Texas, Arizona, 55% of our 28-hospital footprint—we've secured value-based contracts like HCA's with UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross Blue Shield. Bundled pilots for joint replacements and spinal fusions cut readmissions 18%, lifting CMI to 1.91 and adding $45 million to Q2 top-line, or 60 basis points to margin. AI tools from Waystar reduced denials from 12% to 8%, recovering $28 million year-to-date. In the Northeast, we achieved 3.1% revenue per discharge growth despite NY reimbursement pressures.

Supply chain efforts dropped supplies to 14.3% of revenue, a 120 basis point improvement via Vizient GPO consolidation at 92% sourcing. Renegotiated ortho and cardio contracts saved 11-15%—like on Stryker Mako—annualizing $62 million. Just-in-time inventory with McKesson cut carrying costs 22%, freeing $15 million. 340B optimization added 25 basis points on stents. This contributed 90 basis points to Q2 margin.

Labor productivity saw expense growth of just 2.8% year-over-year despite 4.1% volume growth, holding labor at 45.2%. Agency RN usage fell to 5% via "CorePlus" pool and capped travel contracts. Hours per CMI-adjusted day dropped 6% to 5.8, ALOS to 4.3 days. In Midwest union areas, flexible per diem pools stabilized costs.

Clinical efficiency features Epic AI across 85% of facilities, cutting no-shows 14% and adding 1,200 cases. Telemedicine at 22% of outpatient, ASC acquisitions targeting 20% margins. Robotics at 28%, LEAN Six Sigma saved $34 million.

These are part of "Margin 15," with Q3 at 12.0-12.4%, full-year 11.2-11.6%.

Building on that, let's look at operating margin by segment. Company-wide, we hit 14.2% in Q2, up 210 basis points year-over-year, sixth straight quarter of expansion from outpatient shift, labor management, and efficiencies. Calculated as adjusted operating income over net patient revenues.

Acute Care Hospitals, 72% of revenues at $2.8 billion, posted 11.8%, up 180 basis points, with admissions up 3.2% to 145,000, CMI 1.68. Revenue per admission up 2.8% from IPPS and contracts. Labor flat at 48%, supplies better 150 basis points via Vizient. Southeast at 13.2%, Midwest 9.5%.

ASCs, 15% at $580 million, 28.4% margin, volumes up 12% to 220,000, revenue per case 5.2%. Labor 32%, OR utilization 92% via LeanTaaS. Sunbelt at 31%.

Behavioral Health, 8% at $310 million, 9.6% up 320 basis points, days up 8%, revenue per day 4.1%. LOS down 10%, turnover to 18%. West at 12.1%.

Physician Services, 5% at $195 million, 18.7%, volumes up 11%, $25 million recovered via Waystar.

On track for 14% full-year, upside from robotics, genomics.

Next, the impact of acuity mix changes on revenue. Our CMI rose 4.2% to 1.78, high-acuity at 32% of volume, adding $42 million or 180 basis points to growth. Each 0.1 CMI point adds $8-10 million.

Driven by demographics in Southeast/Sunbelt, 60% beds, 7% high-acuity Medicare rise. Florida CMI 1.85 from heart failure. Post-pandemic sepsis up 9%. Northeast flat, Midwest/Southwest up 5-6%.

Proactive: CDI with 3M/Nuance added $15 million, service-line focus to 28% revenues, tele-ICU cut LOS 0.8 days. FY24 CMI 1.76-1.80, $150-180 million uplift.

Revenue per admission trends at $14,820, up 5.8% year-over-year from $13,990, sequential 1.2%. TTM $14,710, guiding $14,900-$15,100.

CAGR 4.1% past five years. Drivers: payer mix to 56% commercial ($22,400 RPA, +7.1%), CMI 1.82, service lines like ortho $28,500. Tech: Epic CDI, Waystar. Sunbelt led 7.2% growth.

Outlook 4-6% sustained.

On M&A, $425 million Tri-State acquisition closed April, $320 million revenue, 22% EBITDA, $18 million synergies. $180 million Phoenix tuck-in Q4 close. Pipeline $1.2 billion, home health $300 million.

Divestitures: $95 million Ohio sale, $65 million proceeds deleveraged to 3.1x. Two more LOI $65 million.

Positions for 8-10% growth.

Same-facility guidance: Q1 2025 admissions 2.5-3.5%, surgical 4-5%, days 1.5-2.5%, ED 3-4%. Full-year 3-4%, outpatient 5.5-6.5%. Revenue Q1 4-5%, full 4.5-5.5%.

Sunbelt stronger.

Strategic priorities: operational excellence, growth, digital transformation. 2024 capex $450 million, tuck-ins $300 million. Admissions 4-6%, revenue 5.5-7.5%. Epic rollout, telehealth to 22%. Q1 EBITDA $460-485 million, full-year $1.95-2.05 billion.

Factors affecting margins: revenue up 7.8% to $2.45 billion, CMI 1.92, outpatient 11.5%. Costs up 5.1%, HAPD down 3.1%, agency 28% less, GPO $42 million savings. Q3 11.0-11.5%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant strides in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Heart Failure Management Program has shown remarkable results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, remote patient monitoring programs, and AI-powered diagnostic tools.

Following that, Tom Hargrove will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including LEAN Six Sigma processes and AI-driven predictive staffing models, which have resulted in significant cost savings, improved patient flow, and enhanced staff productivity.

Next, Karen Walsh will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Karen Walsh:
Thank you, Tom. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets, enhance our service offerings, and diversify our revenue streams.

After that, Raj Singh will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Karen. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture, ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, and mitigate the risk of data breaches. We are also investing in cloud-based solutions to improve scalability and flexibility.

Following that, David Lee will discuss our efforts related to workforce development and employee engagement.

David Lee:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly skilled and engaged workforce. We are implementing several initiatives to improve employee satisfaction, enhance training and development opportunities, and promote a culture of diversity and inclusion.

Finally, Monica Ruiz will elaborate on our compliance efforts.

Monica Ruiz:
Thank you, David. We are dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct and regulatory compliance. We have implemented a comprehensive compliance program to ensure adherence to all applicable laws and regulations, protect patient privacy, and prevent fraud and abuse.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

David Lee:
Certainly, John. We're rolling out competitive compensation packages benchmarked against industry leaders, comprehensive professional development programs including leadership tracks and clinical certifications, and wellness initiatives like mental health support and flexible scheduling. We've also launched employee resource groups to foster diversity and inclusion, resulting in a 15% improvement in engagement scores year-over-year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

Monica Ruiz:
Great question, Maria. Our compliance program includes regular audits, mandatory training across all levels, and real-time monitoring tools for HIPAA and Stark Law adherence. On cybersecurity, we've layered multi-factor authentication, endpoint detection with AI from CrowdStrike, and annual penetration testing, reducing breach risks by 40%. We're also prepared for evolving threats like ransomware through incident response drills.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

Karen Walsh:
Absolutely, David. Acquisitions like Tri-State add scale in high-growth areas, delivering immediate synergies in revenue cycle and supplies while expanding our commercial payer mix. We expect them to contribute 4 points to revenue growth and enhance margins by 200 basis points long-term, positioning us for 8-10% annual growth through vertical integration and market consolidation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thanks, Alex. Our AI tools, integrated into Epic, analyze imaging and labs for early detection—reducing diagnostic errors in oncology by 25% and sepsis by 18% in pilots. We're using predictive algorithms similar to those from Tempus for precision medicine, improving outcomes and CMI while ensuring clinician oversight for ethical deployment.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the HealthSpan Hospitals Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
